result.title: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories
result.comment: 47 pages. Mingyuan Ma and Yangmin Li contributed equally
result.summary: Hybrid language models interleave a few softmax-attention layers with many linear-attention or state-space layers, so every layer keeps a memory of earlier tokens: a key-value cache or a fixed-size recurrent state. Serving them spends more compute and high-bandwidth memory on these memories than the output requires. The prefill runs every layer for every prompt token, and every decode step loads and stores whole recurrent states, which on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next take as many bytes per request as the attention cache of thousands of tokens. We find two properties of trained hybrids that locate this excess. First, writes are easier than reads: writing a deep layer's memory of a token needs little of the deep computation that predicting the next token needs. Trained copies of the deep layers' write paths, which we call emitters, therefore write a prompt's deep memories from the residual stream of a shallower anchor layer, and all prompt tokens but the last run as few as 63% of the layers. Second, recurrent states have a state sink: most of their energy lies in a rank-one term along a fixed direction of each head, and the rest is a low-rank working memory. SEED builds on both: it makes the prefill shallow in depth and the decode state shallow in representation. Each recurrent state is stored as its sink plus low-rank factors, which the Gated DeltaNet, Kimi Delta Attention and Mamba-2 updates extend exactly; we prove that the open-loop error of the periodic compressions back to low rank is bounded independently of their number. SEED keeps the original weights frozen, compresses no attention cache, and runs all layers for every generated token. On six checkpoints of five production hybrids of 30B to over 300B parameters, it is nearly lossless on eleven official exams. Served with SGLang on NVIDIA GB300 GPUs on an agentic-coding trace, it raises the per-GPU throughput of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 1.2-1.4x.

AI.brief_summary: 针对混合注意力/状态空间语言模型的推理成本，论文发现深层记忆的写入可由浅层残差流经「emitter」预测，且循环状态能量集中在固定方向的秩一项上，据此提出 SEED，将 prefill 变浅、把循环状态压缩为 sink 加低秩因子。
AI.relevance_reason: 深层状态可由浅层表示预测、以及状态呈「sink 加低秩工作记忆」的结构，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的跨深度预测、压缩存储与相似度中深度/缓存因素提供核查线索，但需确认压缩是否损失推理所需信息。
